chunks: They were those who, when it was said to them, "There is no god but God," behaved with insolence,

key_terms.لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but God (the core declaration of monotheism)
key_terms.يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ: They behaved with insolence / were arrogant

ai.seo_question: Why did the early disbelievers reject the call to monotheism?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological barrier of *istikbar* (arrogant pride) that prevented the Quraish from accepting the core tenet of Islam, illustrating how ego obstructs spiritual insight. This reaction is often contrasted with the humility of the *Muqarrabun* (those brought near to God), emphasizing that true submission requires the dissolution of self-importance. The verse serves as a warning that rejection of divine truth is frequently rooted in social and personal pride rather than intellectual doubt.
